DILG BAGONG PLIP'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www_dilg_gov-ph OPINION NO. MAY 30 HON. ORLANDO M. JAMILLA Sangguniang Bayan Member Gloria, Oriental Mindoro Dear SB Member Jamillal, This pertains to your letter dated October 19, 2022 requesting for legal opinion on the following: (I) Given the circumstances on the failure to submit before the previous Sangguniang Bayan a Letter of appointment and no confirmation of reappointment occurred of a conterminous official such as the Municipal Administrator, is it sound, proper and legal for the present Sanggunian Bayan member of Gloria, Oriental Mindoro to concur and issue the confirmation letter in favor of the Municipal Administrator for the years 2022 to 2025 despite there are some issues yet to be resolved? (a) 2019-2022 he acted as municipal administrator without concurrence of the previous Sangguniang Bayan of Gloria Oriental Minidoro; and (b) There is a certification of assumption of office from Municipal Mayor effective date October IO, 2022 while Municipal Administrator is acting and receiving salary starting July 2022 up to now. (2) Assuming that the Sanggunian Bayan issued the required Letter of Confirmation, does it have a retroactive effect on the non-occurrence for the previous term, 2019 to 2022? and what are the legal implications to the present Sangunian Bayan Member who gave a confirmation resolution in favor of the request of the mayor despite a knowledge of said issues? (3) What is the legal effect on the transactions, emoluments and salaries the Municipal Administrator received, entered and transacted in his capacity as the MA without the necessary confirmation process? Per your representation, Atty. Mike Ceniza was appointed as the Municipal Administrator (MA) sometime in February 2019 by Municipal Mayor Hon. German Rodegerio in a coterminous capacity and was confirmed by the Sangguniang Bayan. In the midterm election in May 2019, the mayor won and was re-elected for the years 2019 to 2022. As a result, his appointees, including the MA, continuously served for the same position without new appointments and confirmation from the Sangguniang Bayan. Per official records from the Sangguniang Bayan, it was found out that during the term 2019 to 2022, no confirmation letter was served or filed seeking Sanggunian Bayan concurrence in accordance with Sec. 443 (d) of RA 7160. On the other hand, the Civil Service Commission issued Resolution No. 000929 dated 6 April 2000 discussing the "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

effect of non-concurrence of the Sanggunian Bayan on Municipal Administrator where it opined that the submission of said appointment is mandatory it being part of the appointing process; non-observance of this requirement will render the appointment incomplete, hence inefficacious. Hence, the queries. The law is clear. Under Sec. 443 (b)l and (d) of the Local Government Code, head of a department or office in the municipal government, such as a Municipal Administrator, shall be appointed by the mayor with the concurrence of the majority of all Sangguniang Bayan members subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. As mentioned, the appointment was not submitted to the sanggunian bayan for its concurrence. The Sanggunian, as a body, acts through a resolution or an ordinance. Absent such resolution of concurrence, the appointment of petitioner failed to comply with the mandatory requirement of Section 443 (b) and (d) of R.A. No. 71602. The Department has consistently opined that the power to concur of the sanggunian mentioned in the provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991 is intended to determine whether or not the appointee of the Mayor possesses all the qualifications prescribed for the position under Sec. 4803 of the Local Government Code of 1991 and none of the disqualifications provided for by existing laws4. In a similar instance, the Department had the occasion to provide guidance on the matter under Legal Opinion No. 124, s. 20025. The foregoing discussions will also cover the third issue raised for resolution. In reply to your first, second, third, and fourth queries, please be informed that the continued discharge of the powers by Mr. Angeles as Municipal Administrator appears to have no legal basis. A person may assume public office once his appointment is already effective. Appointment to public office becomes effective only once it is completed. The Supreme Court in one case (Attv. David B. Corpuz vs. Court of 1 Section 443. Officials of the Municipal Government. - xxx (b) In addition, thereto, the mayor may appoint a municipal administrator, a municipal legal officer, a municipal agriculturist, a municipal environment and natural resources officer, a municipal social welfare and development officer, a municipal architect, and a municipal information officer. xxx xxx (d) Unless otherwise provided herein, heads of departments and offices shall be appointed by the municipal mayor with the concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang bayan members, subject to civil service law, rules and regulations. The sangguniang bayan shall act on the appointment within fifteen (15) days from the date of its submission; otherwise, the same shall be deemed confirmed. 2 Montuerto vs. Honorable Mayor Ty, G.R. No. 177736, October 6, 2008. 3 Section 480. Qualifications, Terms, Powers and Duties. (a) No person shall be appointed administrator unless he is a citizen of the Philippines, a resident of the local government unit concerned, of good moral character, a holder of a college degree preferably in public administration, law, or any other related course from a recognized college or university, and a first-grade civil service eligible or its equivalent. He must have acquired experience in management and administration work for at least five (5) years in the case of the provincial or city administrator, and three (3) years in the case of the municipal administrator. The term of administrator is coterminous with that of his appointing authority. The appointment of an administrator shall be mandatory for the provincial and city governments, and optional for the municipal government. 4 DILG LO No. 11 s. 2016; February 18, 2016. 5 July 29, 2002 Page 2 of 4

Appeals, et. al., G. R. No. 123989, 26 January 1998) held that where the assent or confirmation of some other office or body is required, the appointment may be completed only when such assent or confirmation is obtained. Until the process is completed, the appointee can claim no vested right in the office nor invoke security of tenure. Since the appointment of a Municipal Administrator requires sanggunian concurrence (Section 443 (d), RA 7160) and considering that the appointment of Mr. Angeles was not concurred in by the sanggunian, his appointment never became effective. As such, his assumption and continued holding of the office of the Municipal Administrator find no legal basis. However, Mr. Angeles may claim salary for the services he has actually rendered. As held in one case (Civil Liberties Union vs. Executive Secretary, 194 SCRA 317), a facto officer is entitled to emoluments of the office for the actual services rendered. Here, Mr. Angeles can be considered as a de facto officer. A de facto officer is one who has the reputation of being the officer that he assumes to be, and yet he is not a good officer in point of law (Torres vs. Ribo, 81 Phil. 44). Corollarily, as held in the Corpuz case cited above, the Supreme Court ruled that a public official who assumed office under an incomplete appointment is merely a de facto officer for the duration of his occupancy of the office for the reason that he assumed office under color of a known appointment which is void by reason of some defect or irregularity in its exercise. The Supreme Court in the case of Menzon vs. Petilla 197 SCRA 251, ratiocinated the entitling of a de facto officer to the salary attached to the office by declaring that under the principle of public policy, on which the de facto officer doctrine is based and on basic considerations of justice, it would be iniquitous to deny him the salary due him for services he actually rendered. It is worthy to emphasize along that line that while Mr. Angeles may be entitled to the salary as a de facto officer, the municipality cannot be made liable to pay his salaries. Instructive on this point is Article 169 (I) of the Rules and Regulations Implementing the Local Government Code of 1991 which explicitly provides, thus: "The appointing authority shall be liable for the payment of salary of the appointee for actual services rendered if the appointment is disapproved because the appointing authority issued it in willful violation of applicable laws, rules and regulations thereby making the appointment unlawful" Corollarily, Section 5 of Rule IV of the Omnibus Rules of Appointments and Other Personnel Actions provides, thus: "The services rendered by any person who was required to assume the duties and responsibilities of any position without appointment having been issued by the appointing authority shall not be credited nor recognized by the Commission and shall be the personal accountability of the person who made him assume office" Hence, Mayor Corales shall pay the salaries of Mr. Angeles for the services the latter has actually rendered. Based from the foregoing and as to the first matter, we opine that it would be improper for the sangguniang bayan to concur and issue the confirmation letter in favor of the Municipal Administrator for the years 2019 - 2022 considering that there was no concurrence to speak of with the previous Sanggunian Bayan Of Gloria Oriental Mindoro. For the years 2022 to 2025, we qualify. The same will only be considered legal upon the date of concurrence of the majority of all the sangguniang bayan members to the appointment of the Municipal Administrator within fifteen (15) days from the date of its submission; otherwise, the same shall be deemed confirmed. Page 3 of 4

As to the second issue of the retroactive effect of the Letter of Confirmation, we deny. As a general rule, laws shall be applied prospectively and will only be retroactive under exceptional circumstances. In the case at bar, the Letter of Confirmation is not a law, more so, there is no substantive right or vested right involved in the case. As to the legal implications to the present sanggunian bayan members who gave a confirmation resolution despite knowledge of said issues, the facts and circumstances are insufficient in order for this level to provide substantial guidance on the matter Finally, this opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations narrated from the letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you on this matter. Thank you.
